jobs.title: French Language Expert (France)
jobs.description:
Role Title: French Language Expert (France)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: France, Remote

micro1 is engaging French Language Experts (France) to contribute to a customer’s audio annotation project focused on French as spoken in France. In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. This engagement is ideal for those with extensive experience in language-related fields such as teaching, transcription, editing, translation, or journalism, or any background that demonstrates a deep familiarity with the nuances of French as spoken in France.

Scope of Work

  1. Listen to and analyze multi-speaker conversational audio samples featuring a range of French dialects and accents from France.
  2. Tag audio and speaker metadata, including aspects such as audio quality, background noise, dialect, accent, age, and speaking style.
  3. Edit and correct automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts using French spelling, vocabulary, and conventions as used in France.
  4. Identify and annotate region-specific linguistic features, idioms, slang, and pronunciation patterns such as regional accents and informal speech (e.g., “t’as,” “ouais”).
  5. Ensure all annotations are accurate, consistent, and align with project guidelines emphasizing French distinctions as used in France.
  6. Collaborate with project team members through written and verbal channels to clarify guidelines or resolve linguistic ambiguities.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluent proficiency in French as spoken in France, with a strong command of its regional varieties.
  2. Background in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or related fields.
  3. Demonstrated ability to distinguish between French dialects and accents from France (e.g., Parisian, Southern/Marseillais, Alsatian, Breton, Norman, Lyonnais).
  4. Familiarity with French vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling conventions (including verlan, regional expressions, and English influences).
  5. Meticulous attention to detail and a keen ear for subtle linguistic differences.
  6. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on clarity, accuracy, and collaboration.
  7. Experience in audio annotation or ASR transcript editing is an asset, though not required.

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Ecosystem Development team is seeking a highly strategic, intellectually curious, and execution-oriented leader to help shape and scale Equinix's next generation ecosystem initiatives.


This role sits at the intersection of technology strategy, ecosystem development, business incubation, and go-to-market transformation. The ideal candidate combines the structured problem-solving and analytical rigor of a corporate strategist with the adaptability of an entrepreneur and the technical curiosity required to navigate emerging technologies such as AI, cloud, networking, and digital infrastructure.


This is not a traditional business development role. We are looking for a builder and strategic thinker who can move seamlessly between developing market and technology strategies, building commercialization plans, evaluating ecosystem opportunities, and driving execution of high-impact initiatives.


The successful candidate will thrive in ambiguity, rapidly learn new domains, and help transform ideas into scalable programs, offerings, and go-to-market motions.


Responsibilities

Ecosystem & Technology Strategy

  • Develop strategic recommendations that shape Equinix's ecosystem, partner, and AI growth initiatives
  • Analyze emerging technology trends, customer needs, competitive movements, and ecosystem opportunities
  • Conduct market sizing, business case development, and financial modeling to support investment decisions
  • Build executive-level strategy papers, business reviews, and recommendations for senior leadership
  • Help define long-term ecosystem and technology strategy in support of company growth objectives

AI Ecosystem Incubation

  • Help identify, evaluate, and incubate new AI ecosystem opportunities
  • Support development of ecosystem magnet initiatives and emerging partner programs
  • Translate partner opportunities into scalable business models and repeatable operating motions
  • Develop frameworks for ecosystem engagement, commercialization, enablement, and scale
  • Partner with business development leaders to move opportunities from concept to repeatable execution

Strategic Initiatives

  • Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives that span Product, Technology, GTM, Operations, Marketing, Finance, and Partnerships
  • Structure ambiguous problems and bring analytical rigor to strategic decision making
  • Build operating models, decision frameworks, and playbooks that enable organizational scale
  • Drive initiatives from assessment through validation, commercialization, and scale

Commercialization & Go-To-Market

  • Develop scalable go-to-market models for emerging ecosystem solutions
  • Create repeatable playbooks for partner recruitment, activation, co-selling, and ecosystem growth
  • Define success metrics, performance models, and operational requirements for new initiatives
  • Work closely with GTM, Channel, and Sales organizations to support adoption and scale

Technical & Analytical Leadership

  • Develop deep working knowledge of AI, cloud, networking, digital infrastructure, and ecosystem architectures
  • Translate complex technical concepts into business opportunities and strategic recommendations
  • Build sophisticated financial, business, and operating models to evaluate opportunities and guide decision making
  • Serve as a connective tissue between business strategy, technical teams, and ecosystem partners

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, this individual will:

  • Become a trusted strategic partner across Product, Ecosystem Development, GTM, and executive leadership
  • Help shape key AI ecosystem initiatives and commercialization strategies
  • Build scalable playbooks and operating models that accelerate ecosystem growth
  • Bring greater structure, rigor, and analytical depth to emerging initiatives
  • Translate partner opportunities into repeatable programs and measurable business outcomes
  • Help move strategic initiatives from concept to validated growth engines

Qualifications

Who You Are

  • Naturally curious and energized by learning new technologies, industries, and business models
  • A structured thinker who enjoys solving complex problems
  • Equally comfortable developing strategy and driving execution
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills
  • Able to quickly become conversant in new technical domains
  • Comfortable operating in highly ambiguous environments
  • Known for taking initiative and figuring things out without being handed a playbook
  • Collaborative and influential across organizational boundaries
  • Possess a growth mindset and a strong desire to continuously learn and expand your expertise

Preferred Background

  • 8+ years of experience in corporate strategy, technology strategy, management consulting, venture investing, product strategy, ecosystem development, corporate development, or a related field
  • Experience developing executive-level strategic recommendations and business cases
  • Strong financial modeling, market analysis, and operational planning capabilities
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution
  • Familiarity with AI, cloud, digital infrastructure, networking, SaaS, platforms, or technology ecosystems
  • Experience building commercialization strategies, operating models, or ecosystem programs
  • MBA or equivalent strategic and analytical experience preferred

jobs.title: Distributed Systems Engineer, Multi-Chip Simulation (Mid/Senior/Principal)
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

Running one AI model across many chips is a distributed systems problem: a host and many chips exchanging data over links, waiting on each other, and failing in ways no single chip would. As a Senior Distributed Systems Engineer, you will help us simulate that system before the hardware exists. You will work with the chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams to build the simulators that stand in for the host, the links, and the protocols between chips.

This role is about building and scaling simulation infrastructure, not testing someone else's code. You will own the software architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack, decide how much fidelity each layer needs, and keep it fast enough that distributed software is exercised every day in CI.

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Chip Simulator Design

  • Design and build the simulators for the host-to-chip and chip-to-chip layers of our system, including the drivers, links, protocols, and transfers that connect many chips into one machine.
  • Model the communication fabric, including transfer timing, collectives, ordering guarantees, back-pressure, congestion, and partial failure, calibrated against real hardware.

Architecture and Scale

  • Own the architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack as new chips, interconnects, and deployment topologies arrive.
  • Compose simulators of different fidelity (fast functional, cycle-level, and hardware emulation) into one coherent multi-chip simulation.
  • Scale the simulation from a few chips to full racks while keeping runs fast enough for daily use in CI.

Correlation and Quality

  • Correlate simulated behavior against emulation and hardware measurements, with regression coverage and clear documentation of assumptions and limitations.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience as a distributed systems engineer building and operating software that coordinates many machines or accelerators through RPC, message passing, consensus, or collective communication.
  • A strong understanding of the failure modes of distributed software, including races, partial failure, ordering and consistency, timeouts and retries, back-pressure, and deadlock.
  • Demonstrated experience debugging timing-dependent bugs across hosts, NICs, or accelerators using traces and logs.
  • Experience building simulators, emulators, or test harnesses for distributed or networked systems is strongly preferred.
  • Sound judgment in choosing the right level of fidelity for a question and balancing accuracy against run time.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for tooling and analysis.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain what the simulation shows, what it does not, and what the software or hardware team should change.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with multi-GPU or multi-accelerator inference or training, including NCCL-style collectives, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism, and host-device runtimes.
  • Familiarity with hardware emulators such as Cadence Palladium or Synopsys ZeBu, or with FPGA prototyping.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • You will own the architecture of the simulation stack that lets our distributed software run across racks of chips long before the hardware exists.
  • You will work across chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams on one of the hardest problems in AI inference: making many chips behave as one machine.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is Mid: $160,000-$220,000, Senior: $220,000–$270,000, Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available

Time off and flexibility

  • Unlimited paid time off; we encourage everyone to truly unplug and recharge
  • 13 paid company holidays
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every bullet, we'd still love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Director, Quality Performance Operations
jobs.description:
Company:

AHI agilon health, inc.

Job Posting Location:

Remote - USA

Job Title: ​

Director, Quality Performance Operations

Job Description: ​

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.


The Director, Quality Operations is a hands-on, results-driven operator responsible for disciplined, scalable execution across HEDIS, Stars, clinical quality programs, and the In-Home Assessment (IHA) program. Reporting to the Senior Director, Quality, this role provides operational leadership for the Quality Operations team and directly oversees the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations. The Director serves as the critical connection point between the centralized operations team and regional and market teams, between operations and technology, and alongside the Payor team with our health plan partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, and work gets done. This role is built for a strong operator with a bias for action: someone who brings structure to complexity, holds teams and partners accountable, closes loops, and consistently delivers measurable improvement in quality results.

Essential Job Functions:


1. Operational Leadership and Execution

Lead the day-to-day operating model for enterprise quality programs, including HEDIS, Stars, ACO/MSSP quality initiatives, clinical quality programs, and the IHA program.

Execute priorities set by the Senior Director through annual operating plans, workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Directly manage and develop the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations, and provide leadership across the broader quality operations team.

Serve as the primary liaison between the centralized Quality Operations team and regional and market teams, ensuring enterprise priorities, workflows, and expectations are clearly communicated, adopted, and executed locally, and that market needs, barriers, and feedback are surfaced and resolved centrally.

Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence, including action-item tracking, issue logs, escalation paths, and KPI scorecards, so that commitments are owned, deadlines are met, and open items are driven to closure.


2. IHA Program Oversight

Own end-to-end operational oversight of the IHA program, including implementation planning, workflow design, market readiness, vendor coordination, KPI monitoring, and issue resolution.

Partner with market, clinical, analytics, coding, risk adjustment, and health plan teams to ensure IHA activities support quality and clinical objectives.

Monitor IHA program productivity, completion, quality, member experience, documentation, and downstream outcomes; implement corrective actions when results are below target.

Drive consistent IHA execution across regions and markets, holding vendors and internal partners accountable to targets and ensuring identified gaps and follow-up needs are closed.


3. Quality Program Operations

Ensure operational readiness for HEDIS/Stars submissions, audits, roadmaps and health plan deliverables.

Coordinate enterprise and market-level quality calendars, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across cross-functional teams.

Drive continuous improvement by evaluating workflows, identifying root causes, and implementing scalable solutions.


4. Technology Partnership and Prioritization

Serve as the liaison between Quality Operations and the Technology and Product teams, translating operational needs into clearly defined business requirements, use cases, and success measures.

Lead prioritization of quality-related technology requests and enhancements based on quality impact, operational risk, and timing; maintain a transparent backlog and roadmap in partnership with Technology.

Track delivery of technology work against committed timelines, coordinate user acceptance testing and rollout with operations and market users, and escalate risks or delays as needed.


5. Health Plan Partnership

Work alongside the Payor team to track, manage, and follow up on open health plan items, requests, and deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution.

Attend and actively participate in health plan meetings, including Joint Operating Committees (JOCs) and quality working sessions, to build strong partnerships with health plan partners and drive quality results.

Lead operational discussions with health plans on quality programs, data exchange and supplemental data, gap closure, and quality results; ensure action items from health plan meetings are documented and completed.

Maintain a consolidated view of health plan quality commitments, programs, and incentive opportunities across markets to inform prioritization and resource planning.

6. Stakeholder and Vendor Management

Build collaborative relationships with Regional Quality, Market, Payor, Clinical, Analytics, Coding, Risk Adjustment, Technology, Product, Finance, and other enterprise partners.

Lead operational discussions with vendors and external partners; monitor results against service levels, quality standards, and contractual commitments.

Support materials and deliverables for executive, Board, JOC, CQC, and other governance forums as requested.


Other Job Functions:

  • Understand, adhere to, and implement the Company’s policies and procedures.
  • Provide leadership, coaching, and mentoring to employees and team members.
  • Support hiring, employee reviews, workforce planning, and development activities for the function.
  • Demonstrate excellent communication, customer service, attention to detail, and accountability.
  • Travel as required.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

Minimum Experience

  • Minimum of 9 years of applicable healthcare quality, clinical operations, or program operations experience, including at least 3 years of people management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional quality programs in Medicare Advantage, value-based care, HEDIS/Stars, ACO/MSSP, or a comparable environment.
  • Experience overseeing large-scale operational programs, vendors, KPI tracking, and process improvement; IHA or in-home clinical program experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong working knowledge of Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS, CMS and NCQA requirements, quality measurement, and healthcare operations.
  • Proven track record as a strong, hands-on operator who drives execution, holds teams and partners accountable, and delivers results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
  • Experience partnering directly with health plans (e.g., JOCs, quality program partnerships) and with technology teams on requirements and prioritization strongly preferred.

2.Education/Licensure:

Bachelor’s degree required in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, business, data analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred


Skills and Abilities:

1. Strong operator with a bias for action; able to take ambiguous problems, build a plan, and drive them to completion

2. Ability to manage multiple priorities, workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously with minimal supervision

3. Skilled at influencing and aligning cross-functional, regional, market, and external stakeholders without direct authority

4. Ability to translate operational needs into clear technology requirements and priorities

5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills; uses data to monitor results and drive decisions

6. Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through; ensures open items are tracked and closed

7. Language Skills: Strong communication skills both written and verbal to work with multiple internal and external clients in a fast-paced environment

8. Mathematical Skills: Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

9. Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.

10. Computer Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); experience with project and work management tools preferred


Essential Physical Functions:

These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all the functions of the job with or without accommodation.

Location: ​

Remote - GA

Pay Range: ​

$129,700.00 - $162,100.00

Salary range shown is a guideline. Individual compensation packages can vary based on factors unique to each candidate, such as skill set, experience, and qualifications.

jobs.title: Junior+ Operations Associate | A-Players
jobs.candidate_required_location: Albania, Andorra, Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Guernsey, Holy See (Vatican City State), Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Isle of Man, Italy, Jersey, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Monaco, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Svalbard and Jan Mayen, Sweden, Switzerland, Ukraine, United Kingdom, Åland Islands
jobs.description:
A-Players is a bootstrapped talent and management company: $2M ARR, 8+ years in market, profitable & impact-driven.

We place vetted, trained Business Associates with early-stage US tech startups (Seed to Series A) and run C-Level, Leadership, and Engineering searches for the same kind of founders.

Today that is 50+ associates working with startup teams in New York, San Francisco, and across North America, and a core team of 10 behind them. Operations today is two people, and the daily flow no longer fits in two calendars. We’re adding a third seat. You take over that flow and make it yours.

The role

You’d join as an Ops Associate. It’s a junior role, and we expect you to grow out of it.

For the first weeks you are the helper: you learn how we run things and run them exactly that way. Once the base is yours, you pick your own projects, and if you’re ready for that sooner than we planned, we’ll make room for it.

Growth here is horizontal as much as vertical: when you find the thing you want to do next, we look for a place for it - something most startups our size can’t offer.

From day one, you work inside the environment of US product companies, the tools, the approaches, and the pace they actually run at, with founders on the other end of the process. Our hires have gone to Reddit, Restream, Unstoppable Domains, GRAI, and Poolday, among others, and two companies we hired for at pre-seed are now unicorns. You see how they are run from the inside, not from a newsletter.

The first year is in Ops. After that, we talk.

What you’ll own

Five blocks. You start on the first two with written procedures and the Operations & Systems Lead next to you, and add the other three as you settle in.

1. Associate servicing. Everything that keeps 50+ associates paid, documented and looked after.

  • Offers, NDAs, and the match paperwork for every new associate

  • Reference checks, including the follow-ups when a referee goes quiet

  • Monthly invoices from 50+ associates: collecting them, checking them against the roster, chasing the late ones, preparing the payroll calculation

  • The records: time off, work anniversaries, and events in Airtable, access requests, and confirmation letters

  • Day-to-day questions from the associates about any of the above

2. Team and people admin. The part of ops people actually notice.

  • Birthday and anniversary gifts, get-well and well-being boxes, for associates and the core team

  • Fun meets and team meetups: the idea, the prep, the logistics

  • Business trips and offsites, from flights and housing to the budget

  • Job posts, links, and interview calendars for our own hiring

  • Accounts, invites, and kit for new core-team members; merch when it comes

3. Requests from the Head of Operations. Research and groundwork need a careful pair of hands.

  • Pricing a tool or a service, testing it, and writing up what you found

  • Pulling internal information together into one clean doc or table

  • Formatting and proofreading before something goes to the team

  • Finance groundwork (prep only, no judgment)

4. Ad hoc requests from the team. Small, varied, and each one seen through to the end.

  • Researching a new service or vendor

  • Tidying up fields in one of our systems

  • Putting together a quick team survey and the summary after it

  • Whatever else lands in ops@ and Slack: you triage it, do it, escalate it, or park it, and say which

5. Automation and the Brain. Our processes live as written procedures and AI skills in the Brain, our company knowledge base in GitHub.

  • From week one you work in it with Claude Code: run the existing skills, fix a step that broke, document what you changed.

  • By the end of month two you bring your first automation of your own, for a process you already run.

Most of this runs through AI first: the invoice check against the roster, the document pack, the first draft of every letter. Our Ops team has already built the workflows; you run them, fix what breaks, and by month two you start adding your own. What stays human is the judgment: AI flags the invoice that doesn’t match, you decide what to do about it (example).

We genuinely enjoy it, and we hope you will too.

First weeks and months

Your first 90 days

  • Week 1: You shadow the Ops Team and learn our procedures.

  • Week 2: You take small tasks with feedback on each one.

  • Week 3: You run your first handed-over blocks (associate servicing, team admin) under our procedures and take ad hoc asks from the team.

  • End of month 2: You bring your first proposals to improve or automate the processes you run.

  • End of month 3: You own your blocks and answer most questions yourself.

Who we’re looking for

A junior generalist, and we mean it. This is a new role that replaces nobody, and your CV matters less to us than the way you work. Most of the skills can be junior. One thing has to be exceptional, not just good. Pick yours:

  • You learn extremely fast and pick up context from half a sentence.

  • You are genuinely strong with AI or technical tools.

  • You have real commercial experience (contracts, invoices, clients, e-signature), even a year of it.

Whichever spike you bring, you’ll probably like it here if:

  • You check what AI gives you. When the invoice total it pulled doesn’t match the roster, you catch it before it goes further.

  • A voice note and three scattered messages are enough for you to write a clear task. Nothing has to be repeated or connected for you.

  • AI is how you work, not a tool you’ve tried. You’ve built at least one workflow with it that you still use, and you can show it on a call.

  • You plan your own day, defend your queue, and speak up early when something looks off.

  • When plans change, you adjust without losing the thread.

  • Your English is good enough to read anything we use and write to anyone directly.

  • You are fine with long, careful, repetitive work. Even with AI there is a lot to verify, collect, and put in order. If you need fast context switches, lots of calls or events to feel alive, this is the wrong seat.

You don’t need to know our tools. If you’ve used any CRM, database or banking app at work, you’ll learn Airtable, Brex, TeamTailor and Copper quickly.

It’s an advantage if you’ve been an assistant to a founder, done ops in a startup or an agency, worked in finance or people ops, or anywhere close to IT and product.

What we offer

Let’s get the expected part out of the way first. Remote, full-time, from Ukraine or anywhere in Europe - we’ve been remote since 2018, so there’s no office anyone can summon you to. A fixed schedule in European time, agreed at the start: it can lean toward the evening, it has to overlap with the team calls, and within your hours you’re reachable - a reply within an hour or two, not the next morning. Flexible, with frames. Unlimited time off, agreed in advance - and people actually take it.

That’s the part you’d expect. Here’s what we think you’re actually signing up for:

  • A seat inside the US startup world, without moving anywhere. From day one you work with founders backed by YC, a16z, and Khosla Ventures - in their tools, at their pace.

  • Growth that’s a plan, not a poster. You join junior, and we expect you to grow out of the role: first you run our procedures, then you pick your own projects - and if you’re ready sooner than we planned, we make room. Horizontal counts as much as vertical.

  • An AI-first ops team to learn from. Every AI and productivity tool we use is paid for, plus our internal library of playbooks and templates - you learn on real workflows, not on trial accounts, and by month two you’re already proposing your own automations. It’s in the plan above.

  • Team trips and offsites. The next one is being planned, and that may well be your first project.

  • A team of 10 that likes working together - and after 8 years, that’s not luck.

How we hire

  1. A call with the Head of Operations, your future manager (60 min).

  2. A 30-minute live working session: one small task, done together, with AI on the screen, on your own tools, so we see how you really work with it.

  3. A 30-45 min call with the Operations & Systems Lead: one concrete check on a real case.

  4. A culture conversation with leadership (30 min).

  5. A paid trial week: five days, full-time, real and realistic tasks under our procedures, a plan in the morning and a status at the end of the day. This is where we see your work, so there is no separate take-home test.

Along the way we look at the things from “Who we’re looking for”: what you do with a messy brief, how carefully you check AI’s work, how you handle a real process. Decisions are fast, sometimes the same day. If it’s a match, you’ll hear right away. If it’s not, we’ll tell you straight. Probation is three months and closes early when the results are there. The seat opens as soon as we find you: December 2026 or early January 2027.

Before you apply, skip the formal cover letter. Tell us what kind of work makes you lose track of time, or something you’ve organized that you’re proud of. A few honest lines are plenty.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Portuguese Language Expert (Brazil)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Brazil, Remote

micro1 is engaging Portuguese Language Experts (Brazil) to contribute their deep understanding of Brazilian Portuguese language, dialects, and pedagogy to a customer's project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems.

Scope of Work

  1. Listen to and analyze multi-speaker conversational audio samples featuring a range of Brazilian Portuguese dialects and accents.
  2. Tag audio and speaker metadata, including aspects such as audio quality, background noise, dialect, accent, age, and speaking style.
  3. Edit and correct automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts using Brazilian Portuguese spelling, vocabulary, and conventions (including the post-2009 Orthographic Agreement).
  4. Identify and annotate region-specific linguistic features, idioms, slang, and pronunciation patterns such as regional accents and informal speech (e.g., “cê,” “tá”).
  5. Ensure all annotations are accurate, consistent, and align with project guidelines emphasizing Brazilian Portuguese distinctions.
  6. Collaborate with project team members through written and verbal channels to clarify guidelines or resolve linguistic ambiguities.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluent proficiency in Brazilian Portuguese, with a strong command of its regional varieties.
  2. Background in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or related fields.
  3. Demonstrated ability to distinguish between Brazilian Portuguese dialects (e.g., Carioca, Paulista, Mineiro, Nordestino, Gaúcho, Baiano, Amazonian).
  4. Familiarity with Brazilian Portuguese vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling conventions (including indigenous-language, African-language, and English influences).
  5. Meticulous attention to detail and a keen ear for subtle linguistic differences.
  6. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on clarity, accuracy, and collaboration.
  7. Experience in audio annotation or ASR transcript editing is an asset, though not required.

Eight ProSidian Global Competencies

jobs.title: Executive Assistant, Leadership Team Support - Search Operations
jobs.description:
This is a position within Haldren and not with one of its clients.
This fully remote role helps scale search execution by improving coordination, documentation quality, and communication cadence across consultants, candidates, and clients.
Key Responsibilities
  • Maintain meeting cadence and ensure decisions and next steps are documented
  • Prepare agendas, briefing packs, and follow-up notes with clear action tracking
  • Support process improvements for scheduling, document control, and executive workflows
  • Manage complex calendars, meeting logistics, and travel coordination (as needed)
  • Maintain confidential records, contracts, and correspondence in shared systems
  • Coordinate candidate and client interviews with discretion and precision

Requirements

  • 5+ years supporting senior leaders, ideally in consulting, professional services, or recruitment
  • Advanced calendar management and executive-level coordination capability
  • Proficiency with office productivity tools and executive document formatting standards
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in a professional services environment
  • High attention to detail, with consistent follow-through on deadlines and stakeholder expectations
  • Comfort working with confidential information and applying sound judgement
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote environment with disciplined time management

Benefits

  • Salary range: 460,000 - 600,000
  • Remote work arrangement (South Africa)
  • Opportunities for professional growth
  • Flat management structure with direct access to decision-makers.
  • Open communication environment.
  • Full medical coverage.
Haldren is a recruitment agency that provides services to clients ranging from startups and non profits to multinational corporations. Haldren emphasizes ethical search processes, attentive candidate care, and leadership placements that support long-term client outcomes.
To learn more about the firm and about our candidate services - please visit
US Recruitment Agency, Executive Search & Talent Solutions

Desired Qualifications For Project Controls Manager | Independent Engineering (IE) Advisory Services / Program Governance [DOE0038038] Candidates:

10+ years of relevant engineering, construction, operations, compliance, risk, finance, or energy infrastructure advisory experience; demonstrated work on oil and gas, power, utilities, or large-scale infrastructure projects for owners, lenders, independent engineers, or federal clients.

Education / Experience Requirements / Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, environmental science, construction management, business, risk management, finance, or related field. Relevant certifications such as PMP, CQA, CIA, ISO Lead Auditor, CHMM, CSP, or PMI-RMP preferred.

10+ years of relevant engineering, construction, operations, compliance, risk, finance, or energy infrastructure advisory experience; demonstrated work on oil and gas, power, utilities, or large-scale infrastructure projects for owners, lenders, independent engineers, or federal clients.

Skills Required

Primarily focused on Engineering Services initiatives and aligned with Program Support activities Independent Engineering (IE) Advisory Services / Program Governance Functional Area Activities.

Independent engineering review; U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Loan Programs Office (LPO) - Style documentation discipline; technical due diligence; risk assessment; program-level schedule, cost, change control, earned value, and reporting governance; data room review; information request tracking; report writing; Excel-based analysis; stakeholder coordination; and clear presentation of findings for credit, construction, monitoring, and certification decisions.

Competencies Required

  • Technical judgment; independence and objectivity; analytical rigor; attention to detail; defensible documentation; client service orientation; cross-functional collaboration; issue escalation; quality mindset; schedule discipline; and ability to translate technical evidence into actionable risk, compliance, and financing implications.

Ancillary Details Of The Roles

  • Ancillary role detail: may participate in data room reviews, borrower/contractor interviews, site observations, monthly monitoring meetings, risk register updates, CP evidence reviews, draw package checks, issue closure tracking, and preparation of Independent Engineer reports for DOE, LPO, credit, and program governance stakeholders.
  • The DOE Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) Program represents DOE/LPO-supported financing and lifecycle oversight activities for large-scale U.S. energy infrastructure projects, requiring independent engineering, technical due diligence, credit evaluation, construction monitoring, operational performance assessment, and risk management services to support financing decisions and protect government lending interests throughout the project lifecycle. DOE financing activities that support U.S. energy infrastructure, energy security, domestic production, and strategic energy investments. The financing authority itself would typically be administered through the DOE Loan Programs Office (LPO).
  • The Loan Programs Office (LPO) is the financing arm of the U.S. Department of Energy, responsible for providing Direct loans, loan guarantees, credit assistance, and project finance support for large-scale energy and infrastructure projects in the United States. The LPO evaluates projects from Technical, Engineering, Financial, Commercial, Environmental, Regulatory, Construction, and Operational perspectives before financing decisions are made.
  • Independent Engineering (IE) Advisory Services are needed for complex energy projects. DOE/LPO frequently requires independent technical reviews similar to those used by commercial lenders, export credit agencies, multilateral development banks, and institutional project finance investors. An EDF-style Independent Engineering engagement could include:
  • - Upstream Oil & Gas (Exploration and production | Reservoir development | Drilling programs)
  • - Midstream (Pipelines | Compression facilities | LNG infrastructure | Storage terminals)
  • - Downstream (Refineries | Petrochemical facilities | Processing plants)
  • - Power & Utilities (Generation facilities | Transmission infrastructure | Grid modernization | Energy storage)

Other Details

Role supports NAICS 541330 Engineering Services for Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) Program/Loan Programs Office (LPO) energy infrastructure financing, with work performed for high-impact oil and gas, power, utilities, and infrastructure projects. Outputs must be independent, traceable to source evidence, suitable for lender review, and aligned with technical due diligence, construction monitoring, EPC oversight, completion certification, operations monitoring, and long-term debt-service viability assessment needs.

jobs.description:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.

We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.

Since launching publicly in September 2023, we have scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.

Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.

Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.

What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.

Locations: Remote. Open to candidates in Canada, Mexico, the United States, Brazil, and Colombia.

The Role

You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.

The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.

The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve. Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined. The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.

You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

What you will do

Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.

Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.

Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.

Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.

Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.

Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.

Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.

What you will need

You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.

Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.

You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.

You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.

You understand the accountant channel and how CPAs influence product adoption. Bonus if you have built for or partnered with CPAs directly.

Typically 4 to 10 years of experience. Title is not the point.

We want to hear from you. We value passion, determination, and honesty. If you do not match every line of the spec but you can show us the work, apply anyway. Unusual paths and rare skills are how you stand out at Flex.

Position Title: Contract Instructor - Cybersecurity, Incident Response & Hands-On Training

Area: USA, APAC, EMEA, LATAM

Location/Work type: Remote: Virtual and in-person classes

Do you love cybersecurity and thrive on helping organizations strengthen their security posture and build resilient defense teams? Pluralsight’s Instructor-Led Training (ILT) team is seeking exceptional Independent Contract Cybersecurity Instructors and Scenario Developers to deliver engaging, high-impact training experiences for Fortune 500 clients. This opportunity allows you to lead live, instructor-led sessions both in-person and virtually, empowering technical and leadership teams through interactive Tabletop Exercises (TTX) and competitive Capture the Flag (CTF) events. Pluralsight offers many ILT solutions including: short workshops, 1–5 day classes, immersive security academies, and blended learning solutions. With topics ranging from incident response workflows to hands-on Red/Blue/Purple team exercises, you will guide learners through structured, real-world instruction that drives immediate security impact. With flexible scheduling, competitive daily rates, and the ability to work from anywhere, this role is ideal for experienced security professionals who are passionate about sharing knowledge and elevating teams.

Who you're committed to being:

  • A passionate educator who believes cybersecurity learning should be practical, engaging, and transformational.

  • A confident communicator who can bridge the gap between high-level incident response strategy and hands-on technical skill-building for diverse audiences.

  • A continuous learner who stays current with emerging threats, evolving exploit mechanics, and modern security frameworks.

  • A collaborative partner who works closely with client stakeholders and Pluralsight teams to evaluate security readiness and ensure exceptional delivery.

  • A professional who demonstrates reliability, adaptability, and a strong commitment to learner and organizational success.

What you'll do:

  • Deliver live instructor-led cybersecurity training, interactive Tabletop Exercises (TTX), and Capture the Flag (CTF) events (both virtual and onsite) for enterprise clients.

  • Design industry-tailored threat scenarios, author CTF challenges, and set up vulnerable lab or sandbox environments.

  • Facilitate decision-making workflows, post-exercise debriefs (hotwashes), and technical walkthroughs that reinforce defensive remediation strategies.

  • Stay current on emerging threat landscapes, MITRE ATT&CK TTPs, and industry security standards.

  • Represent Pluralsight professionally while creating an engaging, inclusive, and high-energy learning environment.

  • Actively monitor our Instructor Portal to accept/decline class opportunities and communicate timely with Pluralsight project managers.

Experience you'll bring:

  • 5+ years of hands-on professional experience in cybersecurity (e.g., Incident Response, SOC/Threat Hunting, Penetration Testing, or Security Engineering).

  • 2+ years of experience facilitating technical training, hosting CTFs, or leading incident response tabletop exercises.

  • Deep expertise in one or more of the following areas:

    • Tabletop Exercise (TTX) Design & Executive/Technical Facilitation

    • CTF Challenge Development (Web Security, Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Binary Exploitation)

    • Threat Frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, NIST IR, OWASP Top 10)

    • Incident Response Playbooks, Workflows, & After-Action Reporting (AAR)

    • Offensive/Defensive Tooling & Scripting (Python, Bash, Wireshark, Splunk, Burp Suite, Metasploit)

    • Cloud & Infrastructure Security Sandboxing (Docker, CTFd, Cloud Environments)

    • Strong presentation skills with the ability to engage both executive leadership and technical engineering teams.

    • Experience delivering security-focused workshops virtually and/or in person to enterprise clients is highly preferred.

Requirements:

    • Minimum 5 years of hands-on cybersecurity experience.

    • Minimum 2 years of instructional, training, or workshop facilitation experience.

    • Ability to deliver training sessions virtually and travel onsite as needed.

    • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

    • Reliable high-speed internet and professional home office setup for virtual delivery.

    • Legal authorization to work as an Independent Contractor.

    • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field preferred (or equivalent professional experience).

    • Relevant cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, GCIH, OSCP, CEH, GRID, Security+) are a plus but not required.

Pluralsight provides the only learning platform dedicated to accelerating the technology skills and capabilities of today’s tech workforce. Thousands of companies, government organizations and individuals around the world rely on Pluralsight to support critical technology skill development in areas that are crucial to innovation including artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, software development, and machine learning. Pluralsight provides highly curated content developed by vetted technology experts, industry leading skill assessments, and hands on, immersive learning experiences designed to help individuals skill-up faster.

Physical Requirements:

This role is primarily performed in an office or home office setting and involves standard computer-based work.

EEOC & Accommodations Statement:

Bring yourself. Pluralsight is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with EEOC guidelines and local laws.

If you need an accommodation to apply, interview, or perform essential job functions, please visit the bottom of our website to learn how to request an accommodation. Learn more about our commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in our DEIB Report.

Recruiting Scam Notice:

Please be aware of recruiting scams. We’ll only contact you from an @pluralsight.com email or verified channels. We never ask for sensitive personal info or payments as part of the hiring process. All openings are posted on our Careers page.

jobs.title: RevOps Manager
jobs.description:
About Tiberius Aerospace

Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge Aerospace and Defense company committed to delivering innovative, secure, and compliant solutions for our customers. We specialize in mission-critical technology services for government and private sector customers, ensuring excellence in aerospace systems design, performance, and compliance. To serve our nations with Strength, Honor, and Purpose - forging the systems that defend freedom and shape the future of defense.

Location : Remote, with willingness to travel

Position Overview

Tiberius is seeking an experienced RevOps Manager to own the company's CRM, pipeline architecture, forecasting cadence, and commercial data infrastructure across all programs and geographies.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who can bring structure, discipline, and visibility to a rapidly scaling aerospace and defense business. The RevOps Manager will ensure every lead, account, opportunity, program, customer interaction, and follow-up action is properly captured, managed, tracked, and reported, and will connect that data to how leadership plans, forecasts, and makes decisions.

The ideal candidate is a CRM expert with strong Salesforce experience, a working knowledge of the full revenue lifecycle (BD, capture, proposals, program delivery), and the ability to build scalable systems that give leadership a clear view of commercial activity, pipeline health, program-level opportunity, geographic coverage, and forecasted revenue.

What You'll Do

  • Own Salesforce as the central system of record for all leads, accounts, contacts, opportunities, programs, geographies, and customer activity

  • Build and maintain pipeline architecture spanning business development, capture, proposals, and program-level engagement

  • Design the forecasting cadence: pipeline coverage, stage-to-close conversion, weighted forecast, and forecast-to-actuals accuracy

  • Partner with the cofounders and executive leadership to define how commercial data should be captured, reported, and used in decision-making

  • Build dashboards and reporting packs that give leadership visibility into leads, pipeline, conversion, program-level opportunities, geographic coverage, and revenue forecast

  • Improve CRM discipline org-wide: data quality, consistent usage, clean handoffs between BD, capture, and program teams, and accountability

  • Identify gaps in lead management, CRM usage, pipeline hygiene, and commercial reporting, then build practical solutions

  • Train and support internal users so Salesforce is adopted properly and used consistently across a growing team

  • Be an integral part of an international BD team, interacting and coordinating with other regional RevOps Managers, developing cohesive plans and processes to standardize sales and revenue metrics and optimise sales reporting.

  • Look for innovative ways to fully segment and mobilise Tiberius’ extensive network of leads to support a broad gamut of relationship building and promotional engagement activities.

CRM, Pipeline & Reporting

  • Own Salesforce configuration, data integrity, dashboards, reporting, user adoption, workflow design, and process discipline

  • Build lead and opportunity routing rules across programs, geographies, customer segments, and pursuit types

  • Maintain consistent definitions for lead status, qualification criteria, opportunity/capture stages, and forecast categories

  • Ensure every opportunity has clear ownership, next steps, close dates, value, probability, and supporting context

  • Build reporting views by program, geography, customer, pursuit status, stage, source, value, and owner

  • Support weekly and monthly commercial reviews with clean reporting, accurate data, and clear insight

  • Build scalable CRM architecture that can support continued growth across programs, geographies, customers, and revenue streams

Operational & Cross-Functional Support

  • Partner with leadership to build a disciplined operating cadence around pipeline and commercial execution

  • Support BD, capture, and program teams with CRM hygiene, pipeline reviews, meeting prep, and action tracking

  • Create SOPs for lead management, CRM usage, pipeline updates, reporting, and forecasting

  • Support proposal and capture workflows so opportunities are tracked from early lead through customer engagement, proposal, negotiation, and close

  • Bring structure without adding unnecessary bureaucracy — systems should be practical, accurate, and easy for teams to actually use

What You'll Bring

  • Strong experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or commercial operations, ideally in a scaling company

  • Expert-level CRM experience, ideally Salesforce (admin-level configuration, not just user-level)

  • Proven experience building pipeline architecture, dashboards, workflows, and forecasting infrastructure

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify trends, risks, gaps, and stalled opportunities

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work across executive, BD, program, finance, and technical teams

  • High attention to detail and strong standards around data quality

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced startup or high-growth environment with minimal direction

Preferred

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, or another government-contracting environment, with familiarity with program-of-record language, OTAs, and DoD acquisition pathways

  • Experience supporting business development, capture, or proposal workflows directly

  • Experience building or cleaning up Salesforce in an early-stage or scaling company

  • Experience managing CRM data across multiple geographies or business lines

  • Experience working directly with founders, CEOs, or senior leadership teams

  • Experience creating executive dashboards or board-level commercial reporting

What We're Looking For

  • A true CRM owner who can bring control, structure, and visibility to commercial activity

  • Strong operational discipline with a practical understanding of how leads become pipeline and pipeline becomes revenue

  • Ability to manage complexity across multiple programs, geographies, customers, and internal teams

  • Commercial awareness and the ability to understand what leadership needs to see to make decisions

  • Bias for action, clean execution, and continuous improvement

Growth Opportunity

This role provides the opportunity to build the revenue operations foundation for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense company, working closely with the cofounders to create the pipeline visibility, reporting discipline, and forecasting rigor needed to support Tiberius as it scales across programs and geographies.

Tiberius Aerospace Inc. is an Equal Opportunity employer. The Company maintains policies and practices that are designed to prevent discrimination or harassment against any qualified applicant or employee to the extent prohibited by federal, state and local laws and regulations. By way of example, discrimination on the basis of race (actual or perceived), ethnicity, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, citizenship, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law is prohibited. If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or need an alternative method for applying, you may contact for assistance. Tiberius Aerospace Inc. participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your I-9 Form information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.description:
Description

About the Position

Ox Security secures the AI-driven SDLC from prompt to production. We eliminate critical, real-time risks from AI code generation through cloud runtime by doing what conventional tools can’t: unifying development and cloud context to stop vulnerabilities right at the source. At OX, we’re building the future of cyber security for the AI era. If you’re looking to work on disruptive technology with an amazing team, you belong here.

We’re growing fast and looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our Engineering team and help build the infrastructure that powers our platform at scale.

This is a high-impact role where you’ll work alongside top-tier engineers, designing and building secure, high-performance systems in a fast-paced environment. If you enjoy solving complex technical challenges and want your work to have real impact - we’d love to meet you.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Design and implement scalable backend systems and APIs
  • Collaborate with Product, Frontend, and other engineering teams on system architecture and requirements
  • Optimize performance, scalability, and security of applications
  • Troubleshoot and resolve production issues with minimal downtime
  • Lead code reviews and promote best engineering practices
  • Mentor and support junior engineers
  • Continuously improve system design, reliability, and development processes

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • 5+ years of experience in backend development
  • AI-First Approach – Active and proficient use of AI tools (e.g., Copilot, LLMs) to streamline coding practices, accelerate learning curves, and optimize workflows.
  • Strong experience building scalable, production-grade systems
  • Proficiency in Node.js
  • Experience with SQL and NoSQL databases
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms and microservices architecture
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Passion for writing clean, maintainable, and efficient code

Bonus Points for :

  • Experience in the cybersecurity, SaaS, or Cloud Security domain.
  • Hands-on experience with modern cloud environments (AWS/GCP), Docker, and Kubernetes.

Employment & Benefits Package (via Commit)

We partner with Commit offshore, who acts as our official local Employer of Record, to manage payroll, local compliance, and provide top-tier benefits for our Argentina-based team members:

  • USD-Based Salary: Receive your salary directly in USD, with full flexibility to manage your funds and convert to local currency on your own terms.
  • 100% Remote: Full-time position based anywhere in Argentina, requiring standard daily availability and reasonable working hours overlap with our Israel and EU teams.
  • ﻿Paid Time Off (PTO): 20 Days Annual Leave & 5 Sick Days to support your health and work-life balance.
  • Gifts & Events: Gifts on your birthday & Holidays along with company events to keep you connected and appreciated.

jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint Corporation is seeking a Entry-level Software Developer to support our U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) Integrated Booking System (IBS) program. This role is responsible for developing, enhancing, and maintaining software applications that support mission-critical transportation and logistics operations.The Software Developer will contribute to front-end and/or back-end development efforts, utilizing technologies such as Angular and Java-based frameworks, based on experience and program needs. This position supports sustainment and enhancement activities across the system lifecycle and works closely with senior developers and technical leadership to deliver high-quality solutions.The ideal candidate brings solid software development experience, familiarity with modern development practices, and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, Agile environment.

This position is fully remote.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain software applications and services supporting the IBS program
  • Develop solutions using Java-based technologies and/or Angular front-end frameworks
  • Implement solutions based on functional and technical requirements
  • Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code following established coding standards and best practices
  • Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve code quality
  • Troubleshoot and resolve application defects and performance issues
  • Support integration across system components and external interfaces
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines, supporting automated build, test, and deployment processes
  • Ensure applications comply with security requirements, including secure coding practices and STIG alignment
  • Participate in Agile development processes, including sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation
  • Support testing activities, including unit, integration, and system testing
  • Collaborate with senior developers, QA, DevSecOps, and infrastructure teams to support successful deployments

Qualifications

  • Active Secret Clearance or ability to obtain
  • Ability to aquire IAT Level II certification (CompTIA Security+ CE preferred) within the first 9 months
  • Minimum 1 years of experience in software development
  • Experience with Java development (e.g., Spring Boot or similar frameworks)
  • Experience with Angular (modern versions), TypeScript, HTML, and CSS
  • Experience building and consuming RESTful APIs
  • Experience working in Agile development environments
  • Familiarity with CI/CD tools and DevSecOps practices
  • Experience with relational databases
  • Strong problem-solving, debugging, and analytical skills
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment

Preferred:

  • Experience supporting USTRANSCOM or DoD transportation/logistics systems
  • Experience with cloud-based environments (AWS preferred)
  • Familiarity with containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Experience with microservices architectures
  • Knowledge of secure coding practices and application security tools
  • Experience with tools such as GitLab, Jenkins, Jira, and Confluence

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.

Should DecisionPoint Corporation. or its affiliates and teaming partners wish to initiate pre-employment discussions, you will be asked to complete an employment application and related employment documents.

Must haves

  • Ability to facilitate and gather business requirements and come up with scalable engineering solutions
  • Strong ability to design data models based on business domain use cases
  • Proven ability to write code for the future, with a strong focus on maintainability and testability

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, organizational and time management skills
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively prioritize and manage multiple tasks/projects simultaneously per the objectives/goals of the organization and execute to deadlines

Nice to haves

  • Prior startup experience
  • Experience with Python, JavaScript
  • Experience solving insurance industry / domain related challenges
  • Experience in web technologies and frameworks (JS/TS, HTML, CSS/SCSS, Angular, React, Bootstrap, Node.js)
  • Familiarity with containerization and orchestration technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).

Benefits

  • Full remote flexibility and asynchronous work culture
  • Unlimited PTO and fully paid sick leave
  • Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus HSA and FSA options
  • Additional financial protection and retirement benefits, including a 401(k), company-paid life insurance, and disability coverage
  • A high degree of ownership, autonomy, and the opportunity to help build and shape a growing company
  • The chance to make a meaningful impact while working alongside an ambitious, high-performing team
  • Exposure to the challenges and opportunities of a fast-growing startup environment

Compensation

Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of relevant factors including experience, qualifications, geographic location and other relevant factors.
